overview: The Medford Energy and Environment Committee reviewed municipal sustainability updates and emissions data, coordinated preparations for the upcoming Harvest Your Energy Festival, and discussed strategies to track the city's Climate Action Plan.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: The committee reviewed and unanimously approved the minutes from the previous meeting.

items.title: November Meeting Schedule
items.summary: The committee agreed to schedule their next meeting for November 10th to avoid meeting on the eve of Election Day.

items.title: Administrative and City Updates
items.summary: Brenda Pike presented updates on several city initiatives, including upcoming environmental events, ongoing EV charging station delays, the Electrify Medford program, school HVAC and solar projects, and a regional deep paving grant application.

items.title: Greenhouse Gas Inventory
items.summary: Brenda Pike reviewed the city's greenhouse gas emissions inventory from 2018 through 2024, highlighting a steady downward trend in building and stationary energy emissions.

items.title: Harvest Your Energy Festival Preparation
items.summary: Members coordinated volunteer assignments and promotional handouts for the upcoming festival, and Loretta announced that thin-film plastic recycling firm Obaggo will be demonstrating at the event.

items.title: Climate Action Plan Monitoring
items.summary: The committee reviewed a spreadsheet tracking the city's Climate Action Plan strategies and agreed to dedicate time in future meetings to review individual sections of the plan systematically.

items.title: Project Updates and New Business
items.summary: Members discussed tree canopy decline, rodenticide limitations, plans for a pocket forest at Tufts Park, and established an informal working group focused on zero-waste initiatives.
